links.outcome: Sensitivity and specificity at net-benefit-derived vs Youden index decision thresholds for mammography AI
links.effect: Net benefit threshold raised mean sensitivity from 64% to 87% and lowered mean specificity from 80% to 49%; FP roughly tripled, FN halved versus Youden index threshold.
links.quote: Tables 1 , 2 demonstrate that our decision threshold method yielded an increase in mean sensitivity from 64% to 87% and a decrease in mean specificity from 80% to 49% across all versions of the three AI services.

links.outcome: Sensitivity and specificity after NB versus Youden thresholds
links.effect: Mean sensitivity increased from 64% to 87%; mean specificity decreased from 80% to 49%; McNemar p-values for NB vs Youden were <0.0001.
links.quote: Tables 1 , 2 demonstrate that our decision threshold method yielded an increase in mean sensitivity from 64% to 87% and a decrease in mean specificity from 80% to 49% across all versions of the three AI services.

links.outcome: Standalone AI classifications versus radiologist reference
links.effect: For both Youden and NB thresholds, all McNemar comparisons to ground truth were <0.0001; authors reported classification errors persisted.
links.quote: The AI results differed significantly from the radiologist interpretations, regardless of the threshold determination method, while still exhibiting classification errors.

screen.practice: decision threshold selection using net benefit vs Youden index
screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates and compares methods for setting operating decision thresholds (net benefit analysis vs. Youden's index) on three AI models for mammography screening.
